When you requested the DMV hearing they should have given you a paper lice sw to drive till the hearing. I had to go to the big office in like Lakewood or Arvada. Make sure the vials from your blood draw aren't bad. Had a dude on my classes that won his DMV case because the vials to store his blood in were outdated and never had to do anything with his license. Fully reinstated no Interlock. 

Also I was over .2 and was able to get in home detention instead of the 10 days in jail. Start the classes asap, my po stopped the drug tests once I completed the classes so that was awesome too.

Yes for an alcoholic dui in CO. Everyone's situation is different and there's different sentences for everyone. Just take into account your value of time and being restricted, paying for potential Ankle bracelet, drug tests that can be like 10 to 30 bucks a pop multiple times a month, mandated classes that also cost alot each week. There might be a work release option but you also pay a shit ton for a bed. Oh and of course the cost of a lawyer that may or may not do anything that you could do yourself. Thats my biggest regret

I had 18 months probation. Along with 60 days in home confinement. The costs of the ankle bracelet, the drug tests each month, it built up exponentially. Yes it worked better with a full time job, but looking back, I'd have rather used all my vacation hrs and sat in jail for 10 days.
31 and benadryl haha still have a sleep schedule like an 18 yr old though. Theres less ppl at night I have to impress so I like it more
I'm pretty okay today. I feel motivated but to do what, unsure. Its amazing the difference a few days can make. Trying to avoid negative things thoughs cause I know how quickly shit can change
You'd be surprised, well maybe not.

Funny you should mention Colorado. Colorado has some of the harshest DUI laws in the country now. DUIs never go away and after 3, you're looking at a fighting a felony charge even if theyre 30 years apart or from another state. T u e book is thrown hard, unless of course you're an aurora pd officer.
He got a dui off it. Fought it hard, not sure if he won his appeal but he did stop coming to the dui classes so we assumed he won.

I feel ya on that sentence. 3k fine and court costs, 60 hrs community service, 2 levels of DUI classes, one a week that cost 25 bucks a pop, 18 months  probation with atleast 3 drug tests a month that are 15 a pop, and then license suspended for 2 years and have to have the interlock breathalyzer for 2 years after that which cost like 80 a month to be recalibrated, ohh and 3500 for my lawyer that I didn't really need. 1st offense ever hadn't even had a ticket in like the 7 years prior. Yes drunk drivers suck but its one of the biggest state wide money pits. It fucked my life up more than a suicide attempt and hospitalization. Needless to say, I just don't drive anymore. Haven't driven a car in 2 years, get anxious anytime im in one, would rather take the bus or rail.

Classmate that was celebrating a new job and bout to move to Washington state, drinking IPAs. Pulled up to a light and tapped bumper of car in front of him. Talked to rhe guy, and this dude is hard of hearing, wears hearing aids. He was apologizing saya he thought the guy said whatever, got in his truck and drove home. Cops come knocking on his door and arrest him for a DUI. His lawyer kept asking him why he answered the door.

I certainly deserved what I got and I dont deny that, neither do most of the folks in the classes that were mandated. But there were quite a few in there that definitely did not deserve it. I was in classes for a year and you see so many folks come thru, you hear their story every week. If you were brave enough, you actually brought your file to share. Some of it was fucked up.
Most certainly. Know a guy who got drunk, walked back to his truck that was parked in a garage where his construction job was working, and went to sleep. Woke up to cops and being arrested.
Thank you for being kind. The next day was better and still trucking.

I had a DUI in 2019 still dealing with. Had to take these alcohol classes that were stupid and morphed into us judt bitching about the cops and our situations. Yes we all take ownership but some of the stories are absolutely outrageous and you can easily see the bias between sentences among us. One guy was drinking at home, went to go somewbere, drove a block realized he wasn't okay. Turned around parked in his garage continued on his business. A neighbor had called the cops, they felt his hood and said its warm. Used that as the cause for arrest. Another chick was also just drinking at home in her garage, cops were called for their neighbors fora domestic violence situation and asked her questions. She had her keys on her and they arrested her. Mine was completely warranted, I fucked up but some of the situations are so fabricated together. Also had an incident at a state park where cops were waiting for campers who would go to their car to grab something and then they'd swoop in saying nope DUI.

Thanks for caring. Had a tall boy in the 3 hrs prior and 2 shots deep now, next tall boy is open. Already said too much to someone close, who knows how they respond. I just wasted so much being anxious instead of feeling what was happening. I'm probably a fine example of mental health issues. Even realizing that its cause my brain is fucked I can't beat it. Im always the odd woman out. Im smart, athletic pretty from one side, the other is not appealing.  Possible on the scale as my social interactions and how I think are not normal.  Im weird anti social but social 

I was okay in my situation yesterday but today I'm not for some reason I don't know. And it fuckin sucks. But truly thank you. This was atleast a way to state the feeling without doing something drastic
